corpus_assessment.inclusion_rationale: The official adopted text and EUR-Lex OJ manifestation verify identity, dates and material AI/algorithmic policy passages. Although the title is broader than AI, the dedicated provisions on AI training, algorithmic bias, automated decisions and human accountability satisfy the direct-AI-first rule. The 2018 OJ reproduction is not a new contemporary document.
corpus_assessment.researcher_notes: Historical collection and corpus classifications are AI-assisted researcher assessments, separate from official metadata.

classification_evidence.locator: Header, recitals B and M-N, paragraphs 8, 19-21 and 25-32
classification_evidence.rationale: Recital B identifies AI training, and paragraphs 8, 19-21 and 25-32 make substantive policy requests on algorithmic transparency, bias, automated decision-making, profiling and human intervention. Direct AI substance therefore applies before indirect legal context.

classification_evidence.locator: Header, recitals B and M-N, paragraphs 8, 19-21 and 25-32
classification_evidence.rationale: Recitals F-G and the general considerations address horizontal effects of big-data and algorithmic systems across public and private sectors.

classification_evidence.locator: Header, recitals B and M-N, paragraphs 8, 19-21 and 25-32
classification_evidence.rationale: The resolution is framed around enforceable fundamental rights, data-protection safeguards and judicial redress for automated processing.
